statements.status_notes: gzip's LZH decoder could read past the end of a global buffer when a crafted .lzh file is decompressed after a crafted .Z (LZW) file in the same gzip run, because its left and right arrays kept values left by the LZW decoder. Upstream's advisory https://www.openwall.com/lists/oss-security/2026/08/23/1 gives the fix as clearing both arrays in huf_decode_start(), at the start of every LZH decode. The CVE lists two upstream commits: https://cgit.git.savannah.gnu.org/cgit/gzip.git/commit/?id=63dbf6b3b9e6e781df1a6a64e609b10e23969681 clears the arrays only in one branch of read_c_len(), and https://cgit.git.savannah.gnu.org/cgit/gzip.git/commit/?id=e7378c2d421be6a286922374425680bbe9ad8b7d (the 'better fix') moves the clearing to huf_decode_start(). With only the first commit, the decoder can still follow stale left and right entries while reading the table built by read_pt_len(), before read_c_len() reaches that branch. Both commits are in gzip 1.15; see https://security-tracker.debian.org/tracker/CVE-2026-41992. Alpine lists the CVE as fixed in its own 1.14-r3 (aports main/gzip secfixes), whose patch clears the arrays in huf_decode_start(); the DHI package of the same version string is a different build. In the DHI Alpine 3.23 gzip package, 1.14-r3 carries only the first upstream commit, 1.14-r4 carries the huf_decode_start() clearing, and 1.14-r5 carries both. Disassembled /bin/gzip in every published build on x86_64 and aarch64 (1.14-r2, 1.14-r3, 1.14-r4, 1.14-r5): 1.14-r4 and 1.14-r5 clear two 2038-byte arrays (the size of left and right) on entry to LZH decoding, and 1.14-r5 clears them again inside that branch of read_c_len(); 1.14-r3 clears them only inside that branch; 1.14-r2 has no such clears. The range therefore keeps 1.14-r3 on the affected side.

Upstream's advisory https://www.openwall.com/lists/oss-security/2026/08/23/1 gives the fix as clearing both arrays in huf_decode_start(), at the start of every LZH decode. The CVE lists two upstream commits: https://cgit.git.savannah.gnu.org/cgit/gzip.git/commit/?id=63dbf6b3b9e6e781df1a6a64e609b10e23969681 clears the arrays only in one branch of read_c_len(), and https://cgit.git.savannah.gnu.org/cgit/gzip.git/commit/?id=e7378c2d421be6a286922374425680bbe9ad8b7d (the 'better fix') moves the clearing to huf_decode_start(). With only the first commit, the decoder can still follow stale left and right entries while reading the table built by read_pt_len(), before read_c_len() reaches that branch. Both commits are in gzip 1.15; see https://security-tracker.debian.org/tracker/CVE-2026-41992. Debian lists it as fixed in gzip 1.13-1+deb13u1 (Debian bug #1141443); that update's changelog names its patch 'gzip: don't mishandle .lzh after .Z', the first upstream commit. Both published DHI Debian 13 builds of gzip 1.13-1+deb13u1 carry that patch: on amd64 and arm64 their /usr/bin/gzip clears the two 2038-byte arrays only inside read_c_len()'s branch, right after filling its 4096-entry table, and not on entry to LZH decoding. Open question: whether these builds are still exploitable through the read_pt_len() path that the second commit closes. A build carrying the second commit, or a reproduction against these builds, settles it.
